newsitem.title: UK: N.Korean harvest "disastrous" - British Red Cross.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean harvest "disastrous" - British Red Cross.

text.p: The British Red Cross said on Friday North Korea faced a disastrous shortfall in its harvest, due at the end of October.
It said the shortfall -- affecting mostly rice but maize too -- was worse than expected and left the country seriously short of food.

"The estimated harvest is now in the region of 3.3 million (metric) tons. This is disastrous in a country which needs at least 7.4 million tons to cover all needs," Geoff Dennis, the charity's international director, said in a statement.

Dennis, speaking hours after returning from the region, said North Korea needed the harvest to yield at least 4.3 million tons, calling this "an absolute necessity to feed the population at subsistence level".
Since 1995, when North Korea was hit by its worst floods in living memory, the country has been struggling to avoid widespread famine.
The Red Cross has been carrying out an extensive relief programme ever since and will launch a drugs programme later this month in an effort to prop up the country's failing health sector.
On Thursday, the United Nations food aid agency appealed to Western countries to give more aid to North Korea to meet a shortfall of up to 800,000 tons of food.
The World Food Programme said the entire population was threatened by the famine, made worse first by floods and now by a devastating drought.
Aid officials said millions of North Korean children were suffering from malnutrition and that the crisis was reaching the scale of the Somali and Ethiopian famines.
